data.body:
STATUS AT HANDOFF (session end) -- release NOT complete.

Done:
- Release commit merged via Gerrit (change 2385, commit 4dafd36d2aa1) -- version bump to
  0.13.0, all local gates green (make lint/typecheck/test, build, twine check).
- release.yml dispatched (run 33273822041): Publish to PyPI -- SUCCESS (nava-rebar 0.13.0 is
  live). Create GitHub Release -- SUCCESS (v0.13.0 tag + release exist).
- Publish to MCP Registry FAILED in that same run: server.json description (190 chars)
  exceeded the registry's <=100 char limit. Filed + fixed as bug lime-nonangelic-agama
  (9497-da35-e247-4cb5): shortened description to 97 chars, added a
  check_mcp_registry_description guard to scripts/release_guards.py wired into release.yml's
  authorize job, added unit tests. Landed via Gerrit change 2387, commit af915ac63bb1.
  Ticket NOT yet closed -- its own AC #3 (attestation that the MCP registry job succeeded) is
  unmet, blocked on the same problem below.
- Bug loathful-unanarchic-chickadee (c21f-6f29-5d2d-4a5a, cross-environment plan-review
  op-cert rejection) confirmed fixed upstream (commit 3bde5613718c); never explicitly closed
  by this session.

BLOCKED / UNRESOLVED -- MCP Registry still does not report 0.13.0:
- mcp_registry job has `needs: [publish, mcp_verify]`; it only runs if Publish to PyPI
  succeeds in the SAME workflow run. A fresh release.yml dispatch (run 33276624345, from
  main after the description fix merged) reached Authorize (passed, confirming the new guard
  works) but Publish to PyPI failed with `400 File already exists` -- PyPI is immutable and
  0.13.0 is already published from the first run -- so Create GitHub Release and Publish to
  MCP Registry were both skipped.
- Confirmed via `gh run rerun --failed` on the ORIGINAL run that job-level reruns pin to the
  ORIGINAL triggering SHA (pre-fix server.json), so that path can't pick up the fix either.
- Tested whether a skipped-due-to-failed-dependency job can be individually rerun
  (`POST .../jobs/<id>/rerun` on the fresh run's skipped mcp_registry job, which already has
  the fix in its tree) -- no-op; GitHub does not support this.
- Tried the documented manual fallback (docs/releasing.md section 4: `mcp-publisher login
  github` + `mcp-publisher publish`) as a same-content, no-code-change path. Login succeeded
  (device flow, twice). Publish failed both times with HTTP 403: registry only recognizes
  io.github.JoeOakhartNava/*, not io.github.navapbc/*, despite navapbc public membership
  being confirmed via GitHub's API (`orgs/navapbc/public_members/JoeOakhartNava` -> 204, and
  present in the unauthenticated public_members list). This points to navapbc's GitHub
  OAuth-App org-access policy blocking the mcp-publisher device-flow app -- requires a
  navapbc org admin with admin:org scope to inspect/approve (Settings -> Third-party Access);
  could not diagnose or resolve this further without that access.
- Net effect: within the existing, already-configured release.yml + documented manual
  fallback, there is currently no way to get MCP Registry publish to complete for 0.13.0
  without either (a) an org admin resolving the OAuth App access restriction so the manual
  fallback can complete, or (b) a change to release.yml's publish/mcp_registry job graph
  (out of scope per operator direction this session).

Remaining unmet acceptance criteria on this ticket: MCP Registry version check, PEP 740
attestation verification, GitHub Release Latest+artifacts verification, Homebrew tap check,
channel-install probe, final receipts. None of these were reached after the MCP Registry
blocker above.

Handing off incomplete. Next operator should either resolve the navapbc OAuth-App access
policy (then retry the manual `mcp-publisher login github` + `publish` fallback with the
current server.json, already correct at 97 chars) or decide on an alternate remediation for
the mcp_registry job graph, then resume the remaining acceptance criteria.
